newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Sanonda net 96 profit up 54 pct.
newsitem.headline: China Sanonda net 96 profit up 54 pct.

text.p: China's biggest pesticide producer, Sanonda Co Ltd, said on Tuesday its 1996 net profit surged 54.11 percent to 77.61 million yuan from 1995's 50.36 million yuan on expanded pesticide output.
The firm's 1996 per-share earnings rose 19.44 percent to 0.43 yuan from 0.36 yuan in 1995, according to the company's annual report published in Tuesday's Shenzhen-based Securities Times.
The company's main operating income jumped 19.06 percent to 774.76 million yuan from 650.72 million yuan, the report said.
Sanonda, based in Hubei province, said it produced 19,118 tonnes of pesticide in 1996, up 25.2 percent from 1995.
Caustic soda output was 43,162 tonnes, up 12.5 percent.
Overseas sales were US$18.72 million in 1996, up 14.5 percent from the previous year, it said.
Sanonda said it planned to pay a 1996 cash dividend of 3.50 yuan for every 10 shares, adding the proposal needs the approval of shareholders.
It said it would present at a forthcoming shareholders meeting its plan to issue 100 million B shares and use the B share proceeds to expand core operations. It gave no further details.
On December 31, 1996, the company said in a statement that it planned to offer 100 million B shares and list the equity in Shenzhen in 1997.
The firm said it would funnel the share proceeds into its core business if the offer is approved by the China Securities Regulatory Commission.

Sanonda said that at the end of 1996, it had total share capital of 181.96 million shares, comprising 84.73 million state shares, 91.81 million A shares, 5.42 million rights shares transferred from state shareholders to public shareholders.
